title: Chronic kidney disease: stage, hypertension and dialysis status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for worsening shortness of breath.

History of Present Illness
The patient presents for follow-up regarding increasing shortness of breath over the past two weeks. He reports the shortness of breath is worse with exertion and has necessitated decreased activity levels at home. He also reports occasional ankle swelling. He has a history of hypertension, which he manages regularly. His current estimated GFR places him at stage 3a.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Furosemide 40 mg daily

Exam
Vitals are stable. Lungs reveal bilateral crackles in the lower lobes. Cardiovascular exam is unremarkable aside from slight bilateral pitting edema noted.

Assessment
The patient presents with symptoms suggestive of fluid overload, complicated by his known hypertension and current renal status of stage 3a.

Plan
Continue current medications, titrating furosemide as needed for swelling. Educate patient on low-sodium diet and weight monitoring. Follow up in four weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.
explanations: Hypertension with CKD is presumed linked: I12.9 for CKD stage 1-4 (sequenced first), plus the N18 stage code.

distractors.why: The classification presumes a link between hypertension and CKD.
I12.0 is for stage 5 or ESRD only.
Stage 3a is documented; do not use unspecified stage 3.
